title: The termwise construction of the derived exchange morphism
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],
$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$
with its natural isomorphism $\theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ of the sheaf-level inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with unit $\eta_u$, counit $\varepsilon_u$). Write $Q$ for the localization functors from cochain complexes to the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; for an edge $u$ of the square write $u^{-1}$ also for the inverse image on derived categories and $\varphi^u_P:u^{-1}(QP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u^{-1}P)$, natural in complexes $P$, for its comparison with the termwise inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; and $Ru_*L=Q(u_*I(L))$, with chosen K-injective resolution $\rho_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}QI(L)$, for the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], on morphisms as in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. For $L\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ ($u:U\to V$ one of $f,f'$), a K-injective complex $P$ on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] and an isomorphism $t:L\xrightarrow{\sim}QP$ in $D(U_{\Et})$, let $h:P\to I(L)$ be the unique homotopy class of morphisms of complexes with $Q(h)\circ t=\rho_L$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; $h$ is a homotopy equivalence and
$$
 \chi_{(P,t)}:=Q(u_*h):Q(u_*P)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ru_*L .
$$
Now let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and let $(I,s)$ be a K-injective resolution of $K$: a K-injective complex $I$ of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and an isomorphism $s:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ in $D(X_{\Et})$ (the class of a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ when $K$ is given as a complex). Let $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$ be a K-injective resolution of the termwise complex $g'^{-1}I$ on $X'_{\Et}$. Then:
(a) the underived exchange morphisms [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] of the terms form a morphism of complexes $\Ex^0_{\square,I}=(\Ex^0_{\square,I^r})_r:g^{-1}f_*I\to f'_*g'^{-1}I$; put $e:=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_{\square,I}:g^{-1}f_*I\to f'_*J$;
(b) with the isomorphisms
$$
 \sigma_{\rm src}:=g^{-1}(\chi_{(I,s)})\circ(\varphi^g_{f_*I})^{-1}:Q(g^{-1}f_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}Rf_*K,\qquad
 \sigma_{\rm tgt}:=\chi_{(J,t)}:Q(f'_*J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K,\quad t:=Q(j)\circ\varphi^{g'}_I\circ g'^{-1}(s),
$$
the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] satisfies
$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}\circ\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(e).
$$
That is, the morphism obtained by applying $\Ex^0_\square$ term by term to $I$ and comparing $g'^{-1}I$ with $J$ is $\Ex_{\square,K}$.

proof.text:
(Representatives of the derived direct image.) Let $u:U\to V$ be $f$ or $f'$, $L\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$, $P$ K-injective and $t:L\xrightarrow{\sim}QP$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] ($I(L)$ being K-injective) the morphism $\rho_L t^{-1}:QP\to QI(L)$ is $Q(h)$ for a unique homotopy class $h:P\to I(L)$, and likewise $t\rho_L^{-1}=Q(h')$ for a unique $h':I(L)\to P$; $Q(h'h)=\mathrm{id}=Q(\mathrm{id}_P)$ and $Q(hh')=Q(\mathrm{id})$, so by the injectivity in that node $h'h\simeq\mathrm{id}$, $hh'\simeq\mathrm{id}$. The termwise functor $u_*$ carries homotopic maps to homotopic maps ([lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] (b), for $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]), so $u_*h$ is a homotopy equivalence and $\chi_{(P,t)}=Q(u_*h)$ is an isomorphism; for $(P,t)=(I(L),\rho_L)$, $h=\mathrm{id}$ and $\chi=\mathrm{id}$. Naturality: let $a:L\to L'$ in $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$, $(P,t)$, $(P',t')$ as above, and $\tilde a:P\to P'$ the unique homotopy class with $Q(\tilde a)t=t'a$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. By the definition of $Ru_*$ on morphisms [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], $Ru_*(a)=Q(u_*\hat a)$ with $\hat a:I(L)\to I(L')$ the unique class with $Q(\hat a)\rho_L=\rho_{L'}a$. Then $Q(\hat ah)t=\rho_{L'}a=Q(h_{P'}\tilde a)t$ ($h_{P'}$ the class $h$ for $(P',t')$), so $\hat ah\simeq h_{P'}\tilde a$ by uniqueness, and applying $u_*$ and $Q$:
$$
 Ru_*(a)\circ\chi_{(P,t)}=\chi_{(P',t')}\circ Q(u_*\tilde a).\qquad(\ast)
$$

(The counit $\varepsilon^D_f$ on a K-injective resolution.) Claim: $\varepsilon^D_{f,K}\circ f^{-1}(\chi_{(I,s)})=s^{-1}\circ Q(\varepsilon_{f,I})\circ\varphi^f_{f_*I}$, where $\varepsilon_{f,I}=(\varepsilon_{f,I^r})_r$ and $\varepsilon^D_f$ is the counit of $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. Put $P=I(K)$, bounded below and K-injective. Property (1) of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction] says, with the identification of $Q(f_*P)$ with $Rf_*(QP)$ used there, which is $\chi_{(P,\mathrm{id})}$ of step 1: $\varepsilon^D_{f,QP}\circ f^{-1}(\chi_{(P,\mathrm{id})})=Q(\varepsilon_{f,P})\circ\varphi^f_{f_*P}$. Naturality of $\varepsilon^D_f$ along $\rho_K:K\to QP$ gives $\rho_K\varepsilon^D_{f,K}=\varepsilon^D_{f,QP}\circ f^{-1}Rf_*(\rho_K)$, and $(\ast)$ for $a=\rho_K$, $(P,\rho_K)$, $(P,\mathrm{id})$, $\tilde a=\mathrm{id}$ gives $Rf_*(\rho_K)=Rf_*(\rho_K)\chi_{(P,\rho_K)}=\chi_{(P,\mathrm{id})}$. Hence $\varepsilon^D_{f,K}=\rho_K^{-1}Q(\varepsilon_{f,P})\varphi^f_{f_*P}$. For general $(I,s)$ let $h:I\to P$ be as in step 1 ($Q(h)s=\rho_K$, $\chi_{(I,s)}=Q(f_*h)$). By naturality of $\varphi^f$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and of the termwise counit [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] (a), $\varphi^f_{f_*P}\circ f^{-1}Q(f_*h)=Q(f^{-1}f_*h)\varphi^f_{f_*I}$ and $\varepsilon_{f,P}\circ f^{-1}f_*h=h\circ\varepsilon_{f,I}$; so $\varepsilon^D_{f,K}f^{-1}(\chi_{(I,s)})=\rho_K^{-1}Q(h)Q(\varepsilon_{f,I})\varphi^f_{f_*I}=s^{-1}Q(\varepsilon_{f,I})\varphi^f_{f_*I}$.

(The unit $\eta^D_{f'}$ on a bounded below complex.) Let $N$ be a bounded below complex on $Y'_{\Et}$. A K-injective resolution $r:f'^{-1}N\to J_1$ exists: with $L=f'^{-1}(QN)$ and its chosen resolution $\rho_L$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $\rho_L(\varphi^{f'}_N)^{-1}=Q(r)$ for a unique class $r:f'^{-1}N\to I(L)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], and $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism because $Q(r)$ is an isomorphism (the cohomology functors factor through $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). For any such $r$, put $t_1=Q(r)\varphi^{f'}_N:f'^{-1}(QN)\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ_1$. Property (2) of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], with its identification $Rf'_*f'^{-1}(QN)\cong Q(f'_*J_1)$, which is $\chi_{(J_1,t_1)}$ of step 1 (for $J_1=I(L)$, $t_1=\rho_L$ it is the identity; for another $J_1$ the comparison $c$ with $cr=r'$ there is the inverse of the class $h$ of step 1), reads
$$
 \eta^D_{f',QN}=\chi_{(J_1,t_1)}\circ Q\bigl(f'_*(r)\circ\eta_{f',N}\bigr),\qquad \eta_{f',N}=(\eta_{f',N^r})_r .
$$

(The derived square isomorphism on complexes.) By [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso], $\theta^D_\square$ is the restriction to $\Dplus$ of a natural isomorphism $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ on $D$, and for every complex $M$ on $Y_{\Et}$
$$
 \theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb},QM}=\beta_2^{-1}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,M})\circ\beta_1,\quad \beta_1=\varphi^{f'}_{g^{-1}M}\circ f'^{-1}(\varphi^g_M),\ \beta_2=\varphi^{g'}_{f^{-1}M}\circ g'^{-1}(\varphi^f_M),
$$
with $\theta_{\square,M}=(\theta_{\square,M^r})_r$ (the isomorphisms $\beta_u$ of that node are the comparison isomorphisms $\varphi^u$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], both being those of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]).

proof.text: (Part (a): the termwise exchange is a morphism of complexes.) By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], $\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ is the transpose under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ of $c_F:=g'^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ\theta_{\square,f_*F}$, i.e. $\Ex^0_{\square,F}=f'_*(c_F)\circ\eta_{f',g^{-1}f_*F}$ (the hom bijection of the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). For the complex $I$ put $N=g^{-1}f_*I$ and $c=(c_{I^r})_r:f'^{-1}N\to g'^{-1}I$; $c$ commutes with the differentials because $\theta_\square$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and $\varepsilon_f$ are natural and $g'^{-1}$ is a functor, and $\eta_{f',N}$ is a morphism of complexes [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] (a). So $\Ex^0_{\square,I}=f'_*(c)\circ\eta_{f',N}$ is a morphism of complexes, and so is $e=f'_*(j)\circ f'_*(c)\circ\eta_{f',N}=f'_*(jc)\circ\eta_{f',N}$.

proof.text:
(Part (b) when $I$ is bounded below.) Assume $I$ bounded below; then $M:=f_*I$ and $N=g^{-1}M$ are bounded below ([lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] (c)). Let $x=\chi_{(I,s)}:QM\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K$, so $\sigma_{\rm src}=g^{-1}(x)(\varphi^g_M)^{-1}$. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] (explicit form), $\Ex_{\square,K}=Rf'_*(b_K)\circ\eta^D_{f',g^{-1}Rf_*K}$ with $b_K=g'^{-1}(\varepsilon^D_{f,K})\circ\theta^D_{\square,Rf_*K}$. (i) Naturality of $\eta^D_{f'}$ along $\sigma_{\rm src}:QN\to g^{-1}Rf_*K$: $\Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}=Rf'_*\bigl(b_Kf'^{-1}(\sigma_{\rm src})\bigr)\circ\eta^D_{f',QN}$. (ii) By naturality of $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ along $x$, step 4, step 2 and naturality of $\varphi^{g'}$ along $\varepsilon_{f,I}$:
$$
 b_Kf'^{-1}(\sigma_{\rm src})=g'^{-1}\bigl(\varepsilon^D_{f,K}f^{-1}(x)\bigr)\circ\beta_2^{-1}Q(\theta_{\square,M})\varphi^{f'}_N
 =g'^{-1}(s)^{-1}(\varphi^{g'}_I)^{-1}\,Q(g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,I})\,Q(\theta_{\square,M})\,\varphi^{f'}_N=w\circ Q(c)\circ\varphi^{f'}_N,
$$
$w:=g'^{-1}(s)^{-1}(\varphi^{g'}_I)^{-1}$, $c$ as in step 5. (iii) Step 3 with $r:f'^{-1}N\to J_1$: $\eta^D_{f',QN}=\chi_{(J_1,t_1)}Q(f'_*(r)\eta_{f',N})$. (iv) Apply $(\ast)$ (for $u=f'$) to $a:=wQ(c)\varphi^{f'}_N:f'^{-1}(QN)\to g'^{-1}K$, $(J_1,t_1)$ and $(J,t)$, noting $t=Q(j)w^{-1}$: the class $\tilde a:J_1\to J$ is determined by $Q(\tilde a)Q(r)\varphi^{f'}_N=Q(j)Q(c)\varphi^{f'}_N$, i.e. $Q(\tilde ar)=Q(jc)$, so $\tilde ar\simeq jc$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; and $Rf'_*(a)\chi_{(J_1,t_1)}=\chi_{(J,t)}Q(f'_*\tilde a)$. (v) Combining, and using that $f'_*$ preserves homotopies and step 5:
$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}=\chi_{(J,t)}Q\bigl(f'_*(\tilde ar)\eta_{f',N}\bigr)=\chi_{(J,t)}Q\bigl(f'_*(jc)\eta_{f',N}\bigr)=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(e).
$$

proof.text: (Part (b) in general: reduction to a bounded below resolution.) Let $P=I(K)$ (bounded below, K-injective), $h:I\to P$ the homotopy equivalence of step 1 with $Q(h)s=\rho_K$, $h'$ a homotopy inverse. The termwise functors $g'^{-1}$, $g^{-1}$, $f_*$, $f'_*$ preserve homotopies ([lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] (b)), so $j_P:=j\circ g'^{-1}(h'):g'^{-1}P\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism, a K-injective resolution, and step 6 applies to $(P,\rho_K,j_P)$. Compare the data: (1) by naturality of $\Ex^0_\square$ [lemma-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-naturality], $e_P\circ g^{-1}f_*(h)=f'_*(j)f'_*g'^{-1}(h'h)\Ex^0_{\square,I}\simeq e$; (2) $\chi_{(P,\rho_K)}=\mathrm{id}$, and by naturality of $\varphi^g$, $\sigma_{\rm src}(I)=g^{-1}Q(f_*h)(\varphi^g_{f_*I})^{-1}=(\varphi^g_{f_*P})^{-1}Q(g^{-1}f_*h)=\sigma_{\rm src}(P)\circ Q(g^{-1}f_*h)$; (3) by naturality of $\varphi^{g'}$, $t_P=Q(j)Q(g'^{-1}h')\varphi^{g'}_Pg'^{-1}(Q(h)s)=Q(j)Q(g'^{-1}(h'h))\varphi^{g'}_Ig'^{-1}(s)=t$, so $\sigma_{\rm tgt}$ is the same. Hence $\Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}(I)=\Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}(P)Q(g^{-1}f_*h)=\sigma_{\rm tgt}Q(e_P)Q(g^{-1}f_*h)=\sigma_{\rm tgt}Q(e)$.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise (kept in substance): the identifications 'g^{-1}Rf_*K computed by g^{-1}f_*I' and 'Rf'_*g'^{-1}K computed by f'_*J' are now named isomorphisms sigma_src, sigma_tgt built from the comparison chi_{(P,t)}=Q(u_*h) of a K-injective representative with the chosen resolution defining Ru_*, and the claim is Ex_K o sigma_src = sigma_tgt o Q(f'_*j o Ex^0_I); stmt_deps gained the notions this uses (Q, derived inverse image with phi, Ru_* on morphisms, K-injective Hom). The one-paragraph imported proof ('forming mates commutes with the passage to the derived adjunction') was not a proof; replaced by 7 steps: Ru_* on arbitrary K-injective representatives (naturality (*)), the derived counit on a resolution from property (1) of prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction, the derived unit from property (2), theta^D on complexes from def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso, Ex^0_I = f'_*(c) o eta termwise, the computation for bounded below I, and the reduction of an arbitrary K-injective I to the bounded below I(K). prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist (unit sk-prop-cd, off route) no longer used: the resolution needed is produced from the chosen one of def-weil-pbc-direct-image.
